credit: Pyro-SDIS, Pyronear association with the French Fire and Rescue Services (SDIS), https://huggingface.co/datasets/pyronear/pyro-sdis
licence_note: Apache-2.0. This is the ONLY corpus the tile classifier is ever trained on. It is French, and the evaluation arms are Californian HPWREN, which is what makes every published FIgLib number cross-network out-of-sample by construction rather than by assertion.
url_note: Shard URL = base_url + sequence_id + '/' + frame. sequence_id is the dataset's own 'data' directory, so the local tree mirrors the remote one and a shard can be checked against the dataset page by path.
catalogue: 33,636 annotated 1280x720 frames from Pyronear cameras: 29,537 train and 4,099 val, published as six train parquet shards and one val shard, 3.3 GB in total.
selection: Every shard the dataset publishes, and no subset: the split is the dataset's own, so choosing shards would be choosing a training set by hand and the val number would stop being the dataset's held-out one.

The val shard is fetched and exploded but never trained on -- scripts/train_tile_classifier.py refuses --split and --val-split that are equal, and the precision/recall it publishes are measured on this split alone.
No FIgLib and no HPWREN path can reach this arm: it is a different continent's cameras, which is the point.
format_note: These files are parquet, not images. Each row carries an 'image' struct of raw JPEG bytes, an 'annotations' string of YOLO 'cls xc yc w h' lines, and an 'image_name'. scripts/fetch.py's explode_pyrosdis converts them into the images/<split>/ + labels/<split>/ tree that the dataset's own data.yaml describes and that scripts/train_tile_classifier.py reads. The exploded tree is derived and is NOT in data/fetch_receipt.json.
sha256_note: Per-file sha256 is not in this manifest, for the same reason as the FIgLib arms: hashing requires downloading. The receipt written by scripts/fetch.py pins what these seven shards contained.
